message.content:
In /bench/repo (the memos Go repo), investigate with thoroughness "very thorough" and report exact file paths and line numbers:

A) User deletion cleanup: when a user is deleted (store DeleteUser in store/user.go and store/db/*/user.go), are their emoji reactions removed? Check: (1) explicit Go code in store/user.go DeleteUser or the API v1 user service DeleteUser handler that deletes reactions; (2) database-level ON DELETE CASCADE rules in store/migration schema files (search LATEST schema .sql files for the reaction table definition and foreign keys, for all three drivers sqlite/mysql/postgres); (3) any Vacuum/cleanup runner that deletes orphan reactions. Report exactly which mechanism (explicit Go code, DB cascade, vacuum, or none) removes reactions of a deleted user, with all evidence path:line — include what the reaction table schema looks like and what DeleteUser does (list every table it explicitly cleans).

B) Profile image (avatar) serving: trace how an HTTP request for another user's avatar (e.g. GET /file/users/{id}/avatar or similar route) reaches stored data. Find the route registration, the handler (maybe server/router/frontend or api/v1 user service GetUserAvatarBinary / avatar handler), each hop: handler -> store.GetUser... -> driver -> avatar bytes decoding (base64 data URI in AvatarURL field?). Give each hop: symbol — path:line.

C) Memo visibility enforcement: find every distinct site in server code where memo visibility (PRIVATE/PROTECTED/PUBLIC) is checked to authorize viewing. Candidates: (1) memo service GetMemo handler in server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go; (2) list memos filter building (default visibility filters in ListMemos); (3) attachment/resource serving (file/attachment binary handler checks related memo visibility); (4) explore/public routes; (5) frontend router memo page? Report every enforcement site with path:line — there are at least three.

Report facts with path:line citations, concise.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Findings.

## A) User deletion → reaction cleanup

**Mechanism: explicit Go code in the driver layer. No DB cascade, no vacuum runner.**

Call chain:
- `APIV1Service.DeleteUser` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:393` (auth check at `:409`, calls store at `:414`; it does NOT touch reactions itself — it only iterates returned attachments for blob-storage cleanup at `:424-438`)
- `Store.DeleteUser` — `/bench/repo/store/user.go:171` (thin: delegates to driver at `:172`, then invalidates cache via `deleteUserCache`, `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go:39`)
- Driver: `DB.DeleteUser` — `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29`, `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:29`, `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:29`. Single transaction: collect targets (`collectDeleteUserTargets`, sqlite `:61`) then `deleteUserTargetsTx` (sqlite `:92`, mysql `:92`, postgres `:92`).

Every table `deleteUserTargetsTx` explicitly cleans, in order (sqlite line numbers; mysql/postgres identical order):
1. `reaction` by `content_id IN (memos/<uid>…)` — reactions *on* the user's memos and comment subtree — `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, sqlite `:96` / impl `:380`; mysql `:96`/`:417`; postgres `:96`/`:380`
2. `attachment` by id — `deleteAttachmentsByIDsTx`, sqlite `:99`/`:390`
3. **`reaction` by `creator_id = ?`** — reactions the deleted user left on *other* people's memos — `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`, sqlite `:102` / impl `:400-403`; mysql `:102`/`:437-440`; postgres `:102`/`:400-403`. SQL: `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = ?`
4. `memo_share` (by creator_id and by memo_id) — sqlite `:105`/`:405`
5. `inbox` by id — sqlite `:108`/`:418`
6. `user_identity` — sqlite `:111`/`:428`
7. `user_setting` — sqlite `:114`/`:433`
8. `memo_relation` (memo_id or related_memo_id) — sqlite `:117`/`:438`
9. `memo` — sqlite `:120`/`:451`
10. `user` row — sqlite `:123`/`:461`

Memo set includes the recursive COMMENT subtree: `listDeleteUserMemoTreeRecursive` sqlite `:133` / postgres `:133` (recursive CTE), mysql uses an iterative loop `listDeleteUserMemoTreeIterative` `:133`.

Reaction table schema — **no foreign keys at all, hence no `ON DELETE CASCADE`**:
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99` (`id`, `created_ts`, `creator_id INTEGER NOT NULL`, `content_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `reaction_type TEXT NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE(creator_id, content_id, reaction_type)`)
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`

The only `FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE` in any LATEST schema is on `memo_share.memo_id`: sqlite `:109`, mysql `:108`, postgres `:108`. `content_id` is a text name (`memos/<uid>`), not an FK, so a cascade is impossible by design.

No vacuum/orphan-cleanup runner exists: `grep -i vacuum` over all `.go`/`.sql` returns nothing; `/bench/repo/server/runner` contains only `memopayload` and `s3presign`.

Test coverage confirming both reaction paths: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/user_service_delete_test.go:188-209` (sets up reactions) and `:287-298` (asserts own-memo and comment reactions gone, a peer's reaction on a foreign memo survives).

## B) Avatar serving hops

1. Route registration: `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121`, avatar route `fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)` at `:124` (group `/file` at `:122`). Wired in `/bench/repo/server/server.go:81-82`.
2. URL is produced server-side: `convertUserFromStore` rewrites base64 avatars to `/file/{users/<username>}/avatar` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:32-38` (`fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name)` at `:36`; `userpb.Name = BuildUserName(user.Username)` at `:17`). So `:identifier` is the **username**, not a numeric id.
3. Handler: `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168`
   - anonymous gate: `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` → `getCurrentUser` → 401 — `:173-181` (`AllowAnonymous` = InstanceURL non-empty, `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go:46`)
   - `getCurrentUser` → `auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` — `:708-712`
4. Lookup: `s.getUserByUsername` — `:185`, impl `:715-717` → `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`
5. Store: `Store.GetUser` — `/bench/repo/store/user.go:148` (ID-only cache at `:149-156`; username lookups go through `Store.ListUsers` at `:158`, which delegates to driver at `/bench/repo/store/user.go:137`)
6. Driver: `DB.ListUsers` — `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:88` (username predicate `:128-130`, `SELECT ... avatar_url ...` `:71-165`, scan into `user.AvatarURL` `:190`); mysql `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go:147`; postgres `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go`. Field: `store.User.AvatarURL` — `/bench/repo/store/user.go:43`
7. Decode: `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` — call `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:196`, impl `:737-750`, regex `dataURIRegex` `:98` (`^data:(?P<type>[^;]+);base64,(?P<base64>.+)`), `base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString` `:744`
8. MIME allowlist `avatarAllowedTypes` — `:75-83` (png/jpeg/jpg/gif/webp/heic/heif), checked `:201`
9. Response: `setSecurityHeaders` `:205` (impl `:758`), Cache-Control `:207`, `c.Blob(http.StatusOK, imageType, imageData)` `:209`

Note: there is **no** `GetUserAvatar` gRPC/Connect handler. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go:25` lists `/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar` in the allowlist, but no such RPC exists in `/bench/repo/proto` or the service — a stale entry.

## C) Memo visibility enforcement sites

Server-side (all distinct sites):

1. **Shared read-access helper** `checkMemoReadAccess` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39`; archived-only-to-creator `:45-53`; visibility gate `:55-66` (non-public → require auth `:60`; private → require creator `:63`). Callers:
   - `GetMemo` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:340`, checks memo at `:356` and the parent memo at `:367`
   - `ListMemoComments` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:148`
2. **ListMemos default visibility filter** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227`: anonymous → `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]` (`:219`); authed, no creator filter → CEL filter `creator_id == N || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]` (`:222`); other user's memos → `[PUBLIC, PROTECTED]` (`:225`). Archived branch restricts to own memos `:188-199`.
3. **File server attachment binary** `checkAttachmentPermission` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650`; unlinked → creator/admin `:652-664`; public + AllowAnonymous → allow `:677`; share_token fallback `:684-689`; private → creator/admin `:699`. Called from `serveAttachmentFile` `:149`.
4. **gRPC attachment access** `checkAttachmentAccess` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422`; public allowed `:445`; unauthenticated rejected `:448-450`; private → creator/superuser `:451`.
5. **ListMemoAttachments** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214-225` (own inline check, not the shared helper).
6. **ListMemoReactions** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30-41`; **UpsertMemoReaction** — `:83` (private → creator/superuser).
7. **CreateMemoComment** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41` (private related memo → creator/superuser).
8. **User stats** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84-92` (ListAllUserStats) and `:217-221` (GetUserStats).
9. **SSE fan-out** `SSEClient.canReceive` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134-142` (private → only creator or admin; unknown visibility denied). Event visibility populated at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go:29-37`.
10. **RSS feeds** — `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:90` (instance feed) and `:141` (per-user feed), both hard-pinned to `[PUBLIC]`.
11. **Sitemap** `getSitemapXML` — `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150`, `VisibilityList: [PUBLIC]`.
12. **Mention/notification targeting** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62`, `:67`, `:84`; email notification body redaction `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go:313,316` and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309,312`.

Deliberate bypass: **`GetMemoByShare`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go:153` performs **no visibility check**; authorization is the opaque non-expired share token (`getActiveMemoShare` `:199`, expiry `:195`), plus an archived/missing check at `:163`. The matching attachment bypass is the `share_token` query param at `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:684`.

Frontend: `/bench/repo/web/src/router/index.tsx` contains no visibility logic — no client-side enforcement (grep for `visibility` under `web/src/router` returns nothing). All enforcement is server-side.
